rename.from: after_create called before associations are saved in rails 4.2.0.beta2
rename.to: after_create on parent is called before associations are saved in rails 4.2.0.beta2

body:
Here is a repository which reproduce my bug : 

https://github.com/osaris/after_create_rails42beta2

you can run the tests to reproduce it `rake test`.

If you rollback to rails 4.1.6 the test is green.

I did reproduced this bug in latest master. I created a Gist using issue reporting template to ease testing for people who want to try / fix this bug. It's available at https://gist.github.com/45200706f5c7df6a5a2e

This was introduced in https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/068f092ced8483e557725542dd919ab7c516e567.

After that commit, _autosaving_ of associations (eg. `comment`) happens with an `after_save` callback, which runs _after_ any `after_create` callbacks (eg. `set_first_comment_id`), hence the failure.

Prior to that commit, the autosave was happening in an `after_create` callback, which was run _before_  any `after_create` callbacks.

However, I'm not sure that the current behavior is incorrect. It was a side-effect but I think it makes sense: saving associated objects (ie. autosaving) happens _after_ saving the parent object and `after_create` happens _before_ `after_save` callbacks, hence before the autosave.

cc @sgrif
I would consider this a regression. 068f092 should be reverted, as the "bug" it fixed was from incorrect usage of callbacks, anyway. /cc @rafaelfranca
Ah I see. Makes sense to revert then, cool.

Can this be related to the infinite loop I am experiencing with a `has_one` model trying to update the parent model on an `after_save`? Test case in https://gist.github.com/rafaelbandeira3/ba9cabfd52193ab300d3#file-test_has_one-rb
@rafaelbandeira3 No, the order for `has_one` and `belongs_to` remain unchanged.
@sgrif Should I prepare a PR with a regression test added?
@agis You should maybe add a test case to ensure this bug doesn't make it again into the codebase

issue.title: Two association records created for has_many through
issue.body:
Given the following class definition:

``` ruby
class Magazine < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :readers, through: :subscriptions
  has_many :subscriptions
  after_create :reader_create
  def reader_create
    r = Reader.new(name: 'auto_created_reader')
    self.readers << r
  end
```

`Magazine.create(name: 'Vanity Fair')` will create one magazine record, one subscription record, and one reader record in the database, as expected.

If you move the after_create call to the beginning of the file:

``` ruby
class Magazine < ActiveRecord::Base
  after_create :reader_create
  has_many :readers, through: :subscriptions
  has_many :subscriptions
  def reader_create
    r = Reader.new(name: 'auto_created_reader')
    self.readers << r
  end
end
```

`Magazine.create(name: 'Vanity Fair')` will create one magazine record, two subscription records, and one reader record in the database.  The subscription records will each point to the same reader, and the same magazine.

I've created a repository with a new Rails project with a single failing test: https://github.com/daveroberts/double_association_record

issue.title: Callback bug where `after_update` runs inappropriately on associated model
issue.body:
I think I've hit a pretty obscure callback related issue.

After creating a record that references an associated model in its `after_create` callback, the associated model's `after_update` callback can be run, even if that model was not updated.

``` ruby
gem 'activerecord', '4.0.2'
require 'active_record'

# This connection will do for database-independent bug reports.
ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: 'sqlite3', database: ':memory:')

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :users do |t|
  end

  create_table :posts do |t|
    t.integer :user_id
  end

  create_table :comments do |t|
    t.integer :post_id
  end
end

class User < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :posts

  after_update :this_should_not_run

  def this_should_not_run
    puts "But it does, even though the user wasn't updated"
  end
end

class Post < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :user
  has_many :comments
end

class Comment < ActiveRecord::Base
  after_create :reference_user

  has_one :user, through: :post
  belongs_to :post

  def reference_user
    puts "If I load my user its after_update callback runs! #{self.user.id}"
  end
end

user = User.create
post = user.posts.create
comment = post.comments.build
comment.save
```

Running the above script will output the strings from both callbacks. The user isn't being touched or modified, just referenced from the comment's callback. If you remove the `self.user.id` call from the comment's callback, the user's callback doesn't run.

The `has_one through` association is required to reproduce the bug. Moving the `after_update` callback to the post model, and referencing the post from the comment's `after_create` doesn't trigger the bug.

My current workaround is to define the `after_create` callback _after_ the comment model's associations. This somehow avoids the `after_update` callback being triggered inappropriately.

I initially hit this bug on 3.2.16, but it looks like it's still present on 4.0.2.

Not sure where to dig in and get started on this, it's pretty obscure. Does anyone have any thoughts?
